On Nov. 5, 1991, unprecedented massive flash floods descended on the city of Ormoc on northern Leyte, killing nearly 4,000 people and leaving about 50,000 others homeless. While passing over the Philippines, Tropical storm Thelma's (Tropical Storm Uring) interaction with the high terrain of some of the islands resulted in torrential rainfall. Through a process known as orographic lift, much of the Visayas received 150 mm (6 in) of rain; however, on Leyte Island there was a localized downpour that brought totals to 580.5 mm (22.85 in). With the majority of this falling in a three-hour span, an unprecedented flash flood took place on the island. Much of the land had been deforestated or poorly cultivated and was unable to absorb most of the rain, creating a large runoff. This water overwhelmed the Anilao–Malbasag watershed and rushed downstream. Ormoc City, located past where the Anilao and Malbasag rivers converge, suffered the brunt of the flood. In just three hours, the city was devastated with thousands of homes damaged or destroyed. A total of 4,922 people were killed in the city alone, with 2,300 perishing along the riverbank.

Ilang mga residente sa mga bayan sa Eastern Pangasinan ang nagbakwit matapos abutan ng flash flood mula sa tubig galing sa bundok at sa water release ng San Roque Dam.

Batay sa monitoring report ng PDRRMO Pangasinan, kabilang mga inabot ng gabaywang na baha ay mga malapit sa Agno River sa bayan ng San Manuel, Asingan, Tayug, San Nicolas, Sta. Maria, Balungao, Rosales, Sto. Tomas, naapektuhan din ang ilang Barangay ng Villasis at Urdaneta City.

Biglang tumaas ang water elevation ng Agno river ilang sandali matapos na magpakawala ng tubig ang San Roque Dam kahapon.

Dahil sa biglang pagtaas ng water elevation ng San Roque Dam sa 278 meters above sea level ng alas dos ng hapon, pagsapit ng alas singko ay mabilis na tumaas ang water level ng San Roque Dam at umabot sa critical level.

Mula sa 1 gate .5 meters opening ay dinagdagan ng NAPOCOR sa 2 gates at 2.5 meters each ang opening sa flood gates na dahilan ng pag-apaw ng tubig sa Agno River at river tributaries.

Dahil dito ay ilang residente ang kinailangang ilikas sa mga evacuation area.

Ayon sa NAPOCOR, nagpakawala ng tubig kahapon ang Ambuklaw at Benga dam na may kabuuang 29.5 meters opening mula sa dalawang dam.

Nasa 4,119 cms ang total outflow ng dam na sinasalo ng San Roque Dam.

Ayon sa PDRRMC, maliban sa dam release, nagdudulot din ng pagbaha  sa mga bayan sa Eastern Pangasinan ang tubig ulan galing sa bulubundukin ng Benguet.

Nagpalatuloy naman ang assessment ng Pangasinan PPO at PDRRMC sa mga naapektuhan ng bagyong Ompong sa lalawigan.

Super Typhoon Rodrigo, 

I still remember the strongest typhoon that hit our town . It was named typhoon Yoling in 1970. During our childhood days, we survey our barrio looking for devastation right after typhoons. If there was less destruction, we were not happy or satisfied. What we enjoy seeing as kids were flattened houses, uprooted trees and logs floating along the Pampanga river for it signals our long wait; floods. And when there’s flood, it means no classes. We don’t care about typhoons then, we enjoyed them. During typhoons, we set out to the rice fields to catch rats and “camaro”. (crickets) not minding the dangers that goes with it. There were no signals 4 back then and  typhoon Yoling was categorised as signal no. 3 although it packs a speed of 250 kmh, a super typhoon now. At 5 years old, I still remember the events that came before and after Yoling........

We were all tuned to the radio before the storm landed. Power was cut and we have to spend the night with kerosene lamps since there were still no emergency lights then. Since our house was the only one built on strong foundations, almost all our neighbours stayed in our house. It was like an evacuation center with people bringing clothes and a little food. The strong winds started at dawn and when day came, you can see the destruction the typhoon brought. The roof of my grandmas house which lies adjacent to ours was swept away 200 meters far. Another house was totally flattened and the road was impassable because of trees and fallen debris. 

At noon, the winds blew stronger. Father was fixing the roof when a flying debris hit his head. Although bloodied, he was still able to fix it sparing our house from further damage. From excitement to fear, from joy to sadness, silence was all over inside the house. We were all under our dining table waiting for worst to come. Once in a while I can hear old people murmuring prayers but the  sound of flying jalousies silenced them. Every time the wind blows stronger their prayers became louder as if competing with the howling wind. After almost 12 hours of pounding, their prayers were answered and Yoling was done with its devastation. 

Storms come and go and the most that they stay wrecking havoc is 24 hours or less. The devastation felt is almost a month or less. Mother would always tell me stories about the great typhoons that hit our town; from typhoon Dading in 1964, Welming in 1967 and Yoling in 1970. But maybe never in her 88 years of existence did she ever thought that a typhoon of such magnitude, wrecking havoc from Mindanao to Luzon, leaving people dead, young and old, raising the price of basic commodities and creating rice shortage would ever come to the Philippines and stay for 6 years. His name is Super Typhoon Rodrigo...........

DENR TO CENTRAL VISAYAS LGUS: REVIEW GEOHAZARD MAPS, MINIMIZE STORM DAMAGE

BY MINERVA BC NEWMAN

CEBU CITY -The Department of Environment and Natural Resources-Central Visayas (DENR 7) urged local government units to revisit the geohazard maps issued to them by the Mines and Geoscience Bureau (MGB-7) on landslides and flooding advisories amid the fury of typhoon Ompong in Luzon and parts of the Visayas.

DENR-7 regional director Gilbert Gonzales on Friday stressed the importance of reviewing the geohazard maps and implement the necessary measures in landslide and flood-prone areas to reduce casualties and damage to property in Central Visayas.

According to MGB-7 regional director Loreto Alburo, preventive actions should be strictly carried out in areas declared as 'susceptible' to either landslide or flooding.

Alburo advised officials to use the information, findings and recommendations provided along with the geohazard maps to enhance disaster risk reduction efforts.

CEBU LANDSLIDE RISKS

Cebu City has 19 barangays that are highly susceptible to landslides, namely Adlaon, Banilad, Buhisan, Budlaan, Busay, Guadalupe, Guba, Lahug, Lusaran, Malubog, Pamutan, Paril, Pulangbato, Pung-ol Sibugay, Sapangdako, Sirao, Tagba-o, Taptap and To-ong, as shown on the geohazard map.

Other areas that are highly susceptible to landslides include Barangays Alpaco, Bairan, Cantao-an, Lanas, Mainit, Mayana, Naalad, Patag, Tinaan and Uling in City of Naga.

Likewise identified as susceptible areas are fourteen barangays in Balamban - Bayong, Buanoy, Cabagdalan, Cabasiangan, Cansomoroy, Duangan, Gaas, Ginatilan, Lamesa, Luca, Magsaysay, Matun-og, Prenza and Vito; seven barangays in Talisay City - Candulawan, Jaclupan, lagtang, Lawaan III, Manipis, Tapul and Sto.Niño and three barangays in Minglanilla - Cadulawan, Cuanos and Manduang.

CEBU FLOOD RISKS

According to Alburo, there are 20 barangays in Cebu City identified as highly susceptible to flooding.

The list includes Bacayan, Cambinucot, Cogon Ramos, Day-as, Guadalupe, Hipodromo, Kamagayan, Labangon, Lusaran, Mabolo, Parian, Pit-os, Pulangbato, San Jose, Sapangdako, T. Padilla, Tinago, Tisa and To-ong;

In Naga City, identified flood-prone areas are Barangays Alpaco, Bairan, Inayagan, Langtad, Lutac, Mainit, Tagjaquimit, and Tinaan as well as 12 barangays in Talisay City,
 Biasong, Candulawan, Dumlog, Lagtang, Lawaan II, Lawaan III, Linao, Pooc, San Isidro, San Roque, Tangke and Tapul and six barangays in Minglanilla, Cuanos, Linao, Pakigne, Tubod, Tungkil and Vito.

BOHOL

In Bohol, areas with moderate to high susceptibility to landslide and flooding inclide the municipalities of Duero, Guindulman, Jagna, Pilar, Sierra Bollunes, Bien Unido, Candijay, Anda, Mabini, Alicia, Loboc, Batuan, Dagohoy, Dimiao and Garcia Hernandez.

NEGROS ORIENTAL

In Negros Oriental, some parts of Ayungon, Jimalalud, San Jose, Sibulan, Tayasan, Valencia, Amlan, Bacong, Dauin, Zamboanguita and Dumaguete City were also identified as susceptible areas.

SIQUIJOR

In Siquijor, municipalities with landslide prone areas are San Juan, Siquijor and Lazi while flood prone areas were identified in all five municipalities of the province.

MAP ACCESS

To facilitate easy access of the geohazards maps, the said maps in a 1-50,000-scale are now available and downloadable in three government websites; www.denr.gov.ph, www.mgb.gov.ph, www.pia.gov.ph, and www.essc.org.ph.
